description: 8 retrieval probes for michalmuskala/jason — Apache-2.0 canonical Elixir JSON library (10 .ex + 14 .exs files). Exercises canonical Elixir patterns: dotted `defmodule X.Y.Z`, protocols (`defprotocol`/`defimpl`), `@behaviour` callbacks, macros for compile-time code generation (`defmacro __deriving__`), bang-suffix function names (`decode!`). Elixir has NO tree-sitter grammar in GRAMMAR_MAP — chunking uses the regex chunker in registry-tooling.js:102-130 (endKeyword='end').

probes.query: decode a JSON string into Elixir terms with Jason
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: `def decode(input, opts \\ [])` (line 68) and `def decode!` (line 89) — the public API for JSON parsing. The defmodule and inner def chunks both produce candidate symbols (`Jason` module-level or `decode`/`decode!` function-level).

probes.query: encode Elixir map to JSON iodata for streaming output
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: `def encode_to_iodata(input, opts \\ [])` (lib/jason.ex line 189) is the public API; the actual iodata-generation work lives in `defmodule Jason.Encode` (lib/encode.ex line 14). Either file is a legitimate top-1 — accept both.

probes.query: pretty-print formatted JSON output with indentation
probes.notes: NL behavior probe: `defmodule Jason.Formatter` (line 1) hosts `def pretty_print(input, opts \\ [])` (line 51) and `def pretty_print_to_iodata` (line 67). Either the module chunk or an inner def chunk is a valid top-1.

probes.query: Jason DecodeError struct raised on malformed JSON input
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: `defmodule Jason.DecodeError` (line 1) — exception struct defined alongside the decoder module. Captured by the chunker's `module /defmodule\s+([\w.]+)/` rule with the dotted form preserved.

probes.query: Jason Encoder protocol for custom encoding implementations dispatch
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: `defprotocol Jason.Encoder do` (line 1) — see EL-007 for the chunker grammar gap. Inner `def encode(value, opts)` (line 74, protocol callback signature) IS captured by the chunker, so retrieval should hit encoder.ex via that anchor.

probes.query: Jason OrderedObject struct with Access behaviour for key-preserving maps
probes.notes: Symbol-anchored probe: `defmodule Jason.OrderedObject` (line 1) with `@behaviour Access` (line 12) — preserves JSON key insertion order using Access protocol callbacks.

probes.query: defprotocol declaration for Encoder type-dispatched JSON encoding in Elixir
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: `defprotocol Jason.Encoder do` (line 1) — KNOWN GAP. The Elixir regex chunker (registry-tooling.js:110-115) has rules for `defmodule`, `def`, `defp`, `defmacro` but NOT `defprotocol` or `defimpl`. The defprotocol block doesn't get its own chunk boundary; retrieval must hit the file via inner `def encode(value, opts)` callback or surrounding context. This is an honest chunker grammar gap.

probes.query: defmacro __deriving__ for compile-time protocol consolidation in Jason Encoder
probes.notes: Grammar-edge-case probe: `defmacro __deriving__(module, struct, opts) do` (line 78) — Elixir's underscore-prefixed special-form macro used by `@derive Jason.Encoder` to generate optimized per-struct encoders at compile time. The chunker's `macro /defmacro\s+(\w+)/` regex matches `__deriving__` since `\w+` includes underscores, and the chunk type is `macro` (not `function` — Elixir distinguishes the two).
